messages.subject: Large effect size range in latent trait GWAS
messages.subject_clean: Large effect size range in latent trait GWAS
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

After a GWAS-by-subtraction, I saw that the effect estimate ranges from -1 to +1 and have become suspicious of this. For comparison with Demange et al, it is the "noncog" GWAS (residual phenotype) that is provided this -1 - +1 est range.

What causes this large range? What should I check for that could be causing this? It is worth noting that there are very small proportions of variants (approx. 0%, eg ranging 6 - 300) are in these extremes, are they just outliers or is this an indication of something being wrong with my analysis?

Best wishes,
Aoife

messages.subject: Rgs between latent GWAS after GWAS-by-subtractions
messages.subject_clean: Rgs between latent GWAS after GWAS-by-subtractions
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have done three separate GWAS-by-subtractions

Subtracting:
Trait 1 from Trait 2
Trait 1 from Trait 3
Trait 1 from Trait 4

After these analyses I wanted to investigate their correlations with the observed (input) GWAS data used and my latent GWAS data. From the LDSC analyses I get weak rgs (rg ranges from 0.09 - 2) between the latent traits even though the variance between them in the model is fixed to 0. These rgs also have significant p-values.

I am struggling to determine what is causing this as I wanted to create latent GWAS that were independent of eachother and this does not seem to be the case from LDSC results.

Any suggestions to check how and why this is happening would be greatly appreciated.

Many thanks,
Aoife
